abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) is an emerging biological and therapeutic strategy that harnesses small molecules or biologics to eliminate proteins of interest by engaging the cellular protein degradation machinery. Here, we report DCAF10 as a TPD-competent E3 ligase. Guided by DCAF10's endogenous recognition of N-terminal acetyl-glycine degrons, we developed an Ac-Gly-Phe-Gly (Ac-GFG)-based recruiter capable of inducing DCAF10-dependent degradation of FKBP12 and multiple protein kinases. Interestingly, the Ac-GFG-based recruiter also exhibited a minor dependence on a secondary E3 ligase, FBXO22, potentially due to metabolic conversion that generates a terminal amine-containing species. Structure-activity relationship studies further identified an optimized N-propionyl-Gly-Phe-Ile (Pr-GFI) motif that enables potent degradation of FKBP12 (DC50 = 1.56 nM, Dmax = 96%) with exclusive dependence on DCAF10. We further leveraged this recruiting motif to develop a BRD9 degrader that induces potent, selective, and DCAF10-dependent degradation. Our findings establish the Pr-GFI motif as a potent and selective DCAF10 recruiter and provide a new chemical handle for expanding the scope of TPD.
authors: Vaz de Castro, P. A. S.
